title: OpenAI rewrites its Model Spec around five core values
subtitle: The updated spec reorganizes behavioral guidance under five commitments, drops most style details, and renames 'the assistant' to GPT.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: On October 29, OpenAI published an update to its Model Spec — the public document describing how its models should behave. The new version is reorganized under five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. OpenAI frames the five as commitments already present in prior versions of the Spec, now surfaced as the organizing frame. The post is explicit that these five are not meant to capture the full range of human values its models should respect.

The structural changes matter more than the headline. OpenAI dropped most of the detailed style guidance that had accumulated across prior revisions and replaced it with added guidance on context, oversight, and agency. It also renamed 'the assistant' — the standard shorthand for the model's role in the Spec — to GPT. The company's own caveat is unusually direct: its models do not yet fully reflect the Spec, and the update describes intended behavior, not a result OpenAI claims to have achieved.

The Spec sits in an unusual position. It is not a regulation, it is not a user agreement, and it is not an alignment research paper, but it is cited in all three contexts. US and EU regulators have treated earlier versions as evidence of self-governance commitments. Alignment researchers at Anthropic, DeepMind, and ARC Evals have used it as a reference for what deployed-model behavior labs are willing to be held to. For developers, it is the clearest public statement of what GPT models are supposed to do when prompts conflict with policy.

A note for learners: the Model Spec is one of the most useful public documents in applied AI, and it is short enough to read in full. If you are building anything on top of OpenAI models — a product, a classifier, an agent — the Spec tells you what the model will do when your prompt and OpenAI's policies disagree. Read it directly, not through summaries. The five values are a frame; the specific examples underneath are where the actual behavior is defined.
